title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Acute neurological deficit.

Vitals:
BP: 138/84
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA

Labs:
WBC: 8.2
Hgb: 12.4
Plt: 210
Na: 138
K: 4.0
Cr: 1.1
eGFR: 65
Glucose: 110

Review of Systems:
Neuro: Pt c/o sudden onset headache and acute weakness. No seizures. No vision changes.
CV: No chest pain. No palpitations.
Resp: No SOB. No cough.
GI: No nausea/vomiting.
MSK: No joint pain.

Social History:
Retired. Lives with daughter. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol.

Family History:
Mother: Hypertension.
Father: Type 2 DM.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 80-year-old female admitted for acute neurological symptoms. Initial CT head showed a spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Managed medically with strict BP control and neuro checks. Pt remained stable throughout stay. Neurological exam showed gradual improvement. Significant deficits resolved prior to discharge. No complications during stay. Pt is ambulatory and stable for home.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
2. Hypertension

Discharge Medications:
Lisinopril 10mg PO QD
Aspirin 81mg PO QD
Atorvastatin 20mg PO HS

Follow-up:
F/u with Neurology in 1 week. F/u with PCP in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, location not named: I61.9 (HCC 248).

distractors.why: It is a hemorrhage, not an infarction.
